activity_context.topic_title: The Gradient as a Normal Vector

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({z}^{2}-xy)-yz$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,-2,0).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({z}^{2}-xy)-yz)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({z}^{2}-xy)-yz)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({z}^{2}-xy)-yz)\,k \\  & =-\frac{y}{{z}^{2}-xy}\text{ }i+(-\frac{x}{{z}^{2}-xy}-z)\text{ }j+(\frac{2z}{{z}^{2}-xy}-y)\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,-2,0) & =-\frac{(-2)}{(0)^{2}-(1)(-2)}\,i+(-\frac{1}{(0)^{2}-(1)(-2)}-0)\,j+(\frac{2(0)}{(0)^{2}-(1)(-2)}-(-2))\,k \\  & =i-\frac{1}{2}\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $i-\frac{1}{2}\,j+2\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0).$
